page: Amazon Web Services m8i.48xlarge is a general-purpose, high-density compute instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors with an x86_64 architecture, it delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core) operating up to 3.9 GHz. The processor architecture includes 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations, and hardware-accelerated cryptography. System memory is provisioned at 768.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Networking capabilities feature a baseline throughput of 75 Gbps. This instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated graphics hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded execution and high memory bandwidth efficiency. In parallel compute assessments, the server scored 207507.41 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 143658.77 in PassMark CPU tests, and 22707.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation, placing all in the top 10% tier. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong sustained throughput, reaching 585.77 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 241.13 GB/sec for writes. Vectorized tasks and compilation similarly benefit from the broad core layout, as shown by Clang software build scores (67256.0) and ray tracing (151976.0). In LLM CPU inference tasks utilizing matrix acceleration, the instance achieves 46.26 tokens per second on text generation using 7B models.

The primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local ephemeral storage, requiring reliance on external storage networks via Amazon EBS. Furthermore, while multi-core parallelism is exceptionally strong, single-core processing metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core result of 2119.09, fall into the middle 50% category. The massive scale of 192 vCPUs provides dense compute aggregation for large-scale enterprise deployments, avoiding the operational overhead of managing multiple smaller distributed nodes.

Amazon Web Services m8i.48xlarge is suited for memory-intensive web tiers, static web serving throughput (reaching 270.13 GB/sec), distributed in-memory datastores (achieving 273.77 million Redis SET operations per second), large enterprise database engines, complex build farms, and CPU-driven machine learning inferencing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores on Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running up to 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) paired with 480 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 extensions. Network throughput is rated at a 75 Gbps baseline, with no local storage or GPUs bundled. Across benchmarks, the instance registers top-tier parallel performance, including 207507.41 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 273.77 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. With an absence of local disks, storage must be attached remotely over the network. It fits enterprise database backends, large software compilation pipelines, in-memory caching systems, and high-throughput static web serving.
